FolderDigest.description: One folder's digest: its direct children counted and XORed.

ForceBody.title: ForceBody
ForceBody.description:
Why a lease is being forced off. Required for a box's lease (a chat's or
a workspace's): the owner or an org admin cuts off a turn in flight, and
the reason goes on the decision row.

FrameAttachRequest.title: FrameAttachRequest
FrameAttachRequest.description:
``POST .../frames``: attach an output frame at the engine's widget hub.
``peer_id`` (the socket's id from its ``welcome``) narrows the frame's
events to that socket; without it they reach every socket of the person.

FrameAttached.title: FrameAttached
FrameAttached.description: The frame's id and the comm-open replays of its model closure.

GpuSample.title: GpuSample
GpuSample.description: One GPU as the box sampled it on its last beat.

GrantEntry.title: GrantEntry
GrantEntry.description:
One line of the permissions answer.

``principal_name`` is the one field here that is not an id or an enum, and
it is filled only on the listing: a share dialog that showed uuids would be
unusable, and the listing is the one place the name discloses nothing —
every row on it is a grant that already exists on a node the caller may
read. It is ``None`` whenever the principal cannot be resolved inside the
caller's org (a deleted account, a disbanded team, a share link), so the
absence of a name never becomes an answer about who exists.

GraphErrorInfo.title: GraphErrorInfo
GraphErrorInfo.description:
A problem in the dependency graph: its code (``multiple_definitions``,
``cycle``, ``syntax``, ``delete_nonlocal``, ...), the name it is about,
and the cells it involves. The one graph error model: ``GraphSummary``,
``GraphView``, the cells of a view and the ``graph`` event all carry it.

GraphSummary.title: GraphSummary
GraphSummary.description:
The document graph (current text): for diagnostics only.

``computed`` is false when the writer had no analysis of exactly the state
it answers for (the platform analyses off the hot path, and the ``graph``
event on the notebook channel carries the analysis once it is ready);
``cells`` and ``edges`` are empty then.

HomeFacet.title: HomeFacet
HomeFacet.description:
Present on a member's home folder, and on nothing else.

A home's stored name is its owner's id — an address, never a label. What a
person reads for it is ``owner_name``: the owner's CURRENT display name,
resolved when the payload is rendered, so a changed name shows at once and
nothing about the account is ever written into the tree. Every surface
that shows a node's name shows this instead when it is present.

InfoResponse.title: InfoResponse
InfoResponse.description:
Build / deployment introspection — what's actually running.

Used by ops to verify which image is live in a customer's VPC without
needing credentials. Mirrors what tools like Sentry or GitHub Releases
expect to see in a `/health` or `/version` endpoint.

InvitationAcceptResponse.title: InvitationAcceptResponse
InvitationAcceptResponse.description:
An accepted invitation and the teams it seated the account in.

``org_team_id`` / ``org_name`` name the organization joined, so a client
whose session is in another organization can offer to switch into it.

InvitationPublicRead.title: InvitationPublicRead
InvitationPublicRead.description:
No-auth preview shape used by the signup page when a token is in the
URL. Returns enough to render 'Join {org}/{team}, invited by {inviter}'
without leaking other invitations or the inviter's email.

`email` is the invited address. Signup against this token only succeeds for
that exact address, so the page prefills it rather than asking the invitee to
retype it; the token was mailed there, so its holder already knows it.

InvitationRead.title: InvitationRead
InvitationRead.description:
Authenticated read shape.

The raw `token` is intentionally NOT exposed — only its keyed hash is stored,
so a DB read can't yield a usable invite link. The recipient's
`/dashboard/invites` page accepts/rejects by `id` (`/{invitation_id}/...`);
the raw token only ever travels in the emailed `/signup?invite=<token>` link.

InvitationRefusal.title: InvitationRefusal
InvitationRefusal.description:
The reason an invitation cannot be accepted, and what would have to
change for it to be — the same sentence the accept route answers with.

InvitationRefusalCode.title: InvitationRefusalCode
InvitationRefusalCode.description:
Why a pending invitation cannot be accepted by the account reading it.

A standing fact about the recipient, not a transient failure: the same
answer comes back on every accept until something outside the invitation
changes. ``other_org`` is the single-org rule — the account already belongs
to a different organization than the one the invitation is into.
``email_verification_required`` asks the account to prove its address
before it joins another organization, and ``membership_deactivated`` says
the organization offboarded this account, which an invitation does not
undo.

InvitationStatus.title: InvitationStatus
InvitationStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an `invitations` row.

`pending` is the only status with effect; others are terminal and exist
for audit. `expired` may be marked lazily on read.

IpInfo.title: IpInfo
IpInfo.description:
Best-effort geo/network context for one IP (external lookup; ``error``
set — and the rest null — when the lookup could not run).

Item.title: Item
Item.description: The one item payload every Files surface returns.

ItemsPage.title: ItemsPage
ItemsPage.description: One page of items, the shape every feed answers with.

JoinMembershipRequest.title: JoinMembershipRequest
JoinMembershipRequest.description:
`POST /auth/memberships/join`: the org whose pending membership the
caller accepts. Checked against the caller's own pending memberships; it
never selects anything else.

JoinOrgRequest.title: JoinOrgRequest
JoinOrgRequest.description:
`POST /auth/refresh/org/join`: the invitation link's token, accepted by a
signed-in person who has no org to enter yet.

KernelEventsBatch.title: KernelEventsBatch
KernelEventsBatch.description: Box -> backend: a batch of a kernel's events, in sequence order.

KernelResult.title: KernelResult
KernelResult.description:
The kernel as the platform last heard of it (``state`` is ``absent``
when it has none), and whether the action was handed on.

LeaseFacet.title: LeaseFacet
LeaseFacet.description:
Carried by the leased folder and everything under it, so a client can
explain why a write would be refused before it attempts one.

1.2.0 names the chat whose folder the lease holds: its id, its current
title, and whether THIS caller may open it. A folder a box is running a
chat in is read-only to a browser for the whole lease, and the browser has
to say which conversation holds it and link there for the people who may
follow the link. The permission is the chat policy's own READ answer,
resolved for the caller by the route; a reader of a file six levels down
who holds no rung on the chat is told the title and given no link.

1.3.0 carries the two names a person reads. ``holder`` and ``machine`` are
both ids when a box holds the folder — the same id twice, in fact, because
a box's lease names itself as both — and a status line built out of them
reads as two uuids. The names are resolved by the route beside the chat's
title, and a surface that has neither says what the holder IS rather than
what it is called.

1.4.0 says whether the holder is serving and how much is still on its way.
``served`` is ``live`` while the lease is streaming and its holder has
beaten recently, and ``offline`` otherwise -- a box that died keeps its
lease until the TTL runs out, and a reader must not be told it is watching
a live machine for those minutes. ``landing_count`` is how many files under
the lease the drive holds an older copy of, or none at all. ``node_id`` is
the leased folder itself, so a surface listing a folder deep inside the
lease can match the lease's own frames without knowing which ancestor
holds it.

1.5.0 says whether the holder acts for the reader. A refusal that names
"someone" when the folder is held by the reader's own chat or box sends
them looking for a colleague who does not exist. ``yours`` is resolved by
the route beside the names, and reads ``none`` on a row it did not resolve.

1.6.0 carries the status the server decided for the folder: live, sync
paused (and why), or a saved copy, with the words to draw it. A reader
renders it and never judges the lease's raw fields itself.

LeaseGrant.title: LeaseGrant
LeaseGrant.description:
What a holder is handed: the epoch it writes under and the cadences it
must keep. The cadences are served rather than compiled into the client
so a deployment can slow them down without shipping a new one.

``inboundPending`` rides every grant — the acquire AND every beat — so a
holder learns that a person dropped a file into the chat without asking a
second question at its own cadence: the beat it already sends is the poll.

LeaseRow.title: LeaseRow
LeaseRow.description: One of my leases, as ``alkera files mounts`` lists them.

LeaveOrgResponse.title: LeaveOrgResponse
LeaveOrgResponse.description:
`POST /orgs/current/leave`: the org the client should switch into next
(the most recently used one the person can still enter), or null when the
person has none left. Nothing is signed in by this answer.

LinkedIdentity.title: LinkedIdentity
LinkedIdentity.description: One linked external-login provider for the current user.

LiveBatchBody.title: LiveBatchBody
LiveBatchBody.description:
One live batch, at most ``files_live_max_batch_entries`` entries long.

The same number the grant hands the holder as ``maxBatchEntries``, read
here rather than compiled in so a deployment that lowers it lowers what it
will accept in the same breath. A batch is one statement per entry inside
one transaction holding the lease row, so an unbounded list is an unbounded
transaction — and the holder is told it sent too many rather than having
them applied.

LiveCadenceWire.title: LiveCadenceWire
LiveCadenceWire.description:
How the holder is told to run the live plane: how long to wait for a file
to stop changing, how often to report, and the three ceilings past which it
must skeleton or defer rather than upload.

Served rather than compiled into the client for the same reason the two
lease cadences are: a deployment that has to slow the plane down — a busy
org, a store under pressure — changes a setting instead of waiting for
every box in the field to update. ``inbound`` is what this folder does with
a write from someone who is not the holder, so a client reads whether to
drain at all off the same block it reads its cadence from.

LiveFacet.title: LiveFacet
LiveFacet.description:
What ONE node is on the machine holding the lease, against the drive.

Present on a node the holder reported (``content``, ``holder_size``,
``holder_mtime``) or one it is moving right now (``state`` and the ``box_*``
pair); absent on every other node, including a folder that merely sits
inside a leased subtree, which carries the lease facet alone.

1.1.0 adds the holder's report. ``content`` is derived per read by
``alkera_core.files.freshness`` and never stored: ``on_drive`` (the drive
has the holder's bytes), ``behind`` (it has an older version), ``unlanded``
(it has none yet), ``unsynced`` (the holder's lease is gone and these bytes
never arrived) or ``none``. ``state`` became optional with it: a file the
holder reported and is not moving has no state, and a default of
``writing`` would have said it was being written.

LiveInboundEntry.title: LiveInboundEntry
LiveInboundEntry.description: One write the drive took into the holder's folder on its behalf.

LiveReportBody.title: LiveReportBody
LiveReportBody.description:
One node as the holder reports it: a stored state, or ``applied`` /
``superseded`` to say the difference the drive recorded is gone.

LiveText.title: LiveText
LiveText.description: The document as a text peer reads it.

LiveTextSubmit.title: LiveTextSubmit
LiveTextSubmit.description: A whole text, and the state it was made on.

LookupPage.title: LookupPage
LookupPage.description:
The readable items among the ids asked for, in the order asked. An id
that does not exist, is another org's, or that the caller may not read is
left out -- the same silence the single read keeps with its 404.

LookupRequest.title: LookupRequest
LookupRequest.description: The ids a client already holds -- the nodes a drop's commits reported.

LostMachineRead.title: LostMachineRead
LostMachineRead.description:
The org machine a workspace ran on that can no longer serve it: deleted,
or out of reach of the person whose chat would run there. ``fell_back``:
a waker that is not a person already moved the workspace to the default
placement, which the workspace's card now shows.

MachineBuyingRead.title: MachineBuyingRead
MachineBuyingRead.description:
Whether the caller's org may buy another machine now, without saying
which plan it is on: ``reason`` is ``plan`` when its plan buys none and
``quota`` when it holds as many as it may.

MachineCard.title: MachineCard
MachineCard.description:
One machine as every surface draws it: an org machine, the shared
machines, a person's own box, or a box a member registered for the org.

MachineClaimRequest.title: MachineClaimRequest
MachineClaimRequest.description:
A platform box claims the machine its credential was minted for. The
kind, size and tenancy come from the credential, never from the box; the
box says only which instance it is and what it can hold.

MachineFaultRead.title: MachineFaultRead
MachineFaultRead.description:
Why a box that answers runs no chat: the server's code and message,
and, for platform staff only, the box's own scrubbed words and when it began.

MachineFaultReport.title: MachineFaultReport
MachineFaultReport.description:
Why the box serves none of the orgs it was asked to: a
``WorkerFault`` code (an unknown one reads as ``other``) and the failure's
own words, scrubbed on the box and again here.

MachineHeartbeatRequest.title: MachineHeartbeatRequest
MachineHeartbeatRequest.description:
What a box says with each heartbeat, all optional: how many chats it
can hold and holds now (how a pool is spread), the daemon it runs, and
whether it has been told to stop and is finishing what it holds.

MachineHeartbeatResponse.title: MachineHeartbeatResponse
MachineHeartbeatResponse.description:
The answer to a heartbeat that carries a body: the machine card, or
``None`` for a box that backs no org machine.

MachineIsolationRead.title: MachineIsolationRead
MachineIsolationRead.description:
How far apart the box can keep the orgs it serves, as its probe found
(``alkera_core.compute.box_isolation``).

MachineIsolationReport.title: MachineIsolationReport
MachineIsolationReport.description:
How far apart the box can keep its orgs, as its probe found. The
profile placement reads is the ``org_isolation`` capability; this is the
detail beside it. Names this side does not know are kept out on read.

MachineMintRequest.title: MachineMintRequest
MachineMintRequest.description: Mint a credential for a box a platform admin provisioned by hand.

MachineMinted.title: MachineMinted
MachineMinted.description:
The one answer that carries the raw secret. It is never stored and
never shown again.

MachineQuote.title: MachineQuote
MachineQuote.description:
What buying an offering at a size would cost the caller's org, and
whether it would be admitted now: the purchase's own rules, decided by the
server.

MachineRead.title: MachineRead
MachineRead.description: The org's workspace machine as the daemon and the machine banner see it.

MachineRegisterRequest.title: MachineRegisterRequest
MachineRegisterRequest.description:
Register a running pod as the org's workspace machine (idempotent by
``provider_pod_id``: registering the same pod twice returns the same row).

MachineReleased.title: MachineReleased
MachineReleased.description:
What a terminate answers: the row as it now stands, plus what the
release did to placement — the orgs whose dedicated assignment named this
machine and who now place by the ordinary rules again, how many of its
chats another box took, and how many wait stranded on it.

MachineRoutingEntry.title: MachineRoutingEntry
MachineRoutingEntry.description:
One chat bound to the machine, as the root process routes it: which
org's process serves it and whether that process should be holding it.
Ids and states only: what the chat says is read by that org's process,
on its own credential.

MachineSpec.title: MachineSpec
MachineSpec.description: The hardware and the customer's rates of one machine.

MachineStateRead.title: MachineStateRead
MachineStateRead.description:
What the machine banner shows for the caller's org: the machine its next
chat would be placed on and that machine's reachability, ``pool`` when a
shared pool box would take it (no id or name: which box is placement's
choice at create time), or ``none`` when nothing would.

``reason`` is the machine's own account of a state that is not ready — the
text a failed provision or a refused start recorded. Without it the banner
can say only that something is wrong, which leaves the reader with nothing
to act on and an admin with nothing to look for. It is never a credential
and never a price: it is the same words the ``compute_machine.changed``
frame carries.

MachineTypeInfo.title: MachineTypeInfo
MachineTypeInfo.description: One provisionable machine type from the catalog, priced for the caller.

MachineUnavailableRead.title: MachineUnavailableRead
MachineUnavailableRead.description:
A wake held because the workspace's machine is gone: what was lost, and
where the opener may wake it instead. ``choices`` are the targets the
opener may move the workspace to (empty when they may not move it), the
default placement first when it serves the org; ``preselect_default`` is
whether the opener is offered it as the answer.

MachineWaitRead.title: MachineWaitRead
MachineWaitRead.description:
Why a machine waits for hardware and when the server asks again, as
the reconcile will act on it.

MachineWorkerCredentialRead.title: MachineWorkerCredentialRead
MachineWorkerCredentialRead.description:
A freshly minted org-bound worker credential. ``token`` is the bearer
the org's process presents; it reaches ``org_id`` and nothing else, and
stops working at ``expires_at`` or the moment the machine credential that
minted it is revoked, whichever is first.

MachineWorkerCredentialRequest.title: MachineWorkerCredentialRequest
MachineWorkerCredentialRequest.description: The org a worker credential is minted for.

MeRead.title: MeRead
MeRead.description:
`GET /auth/me`: the current user plus when their access token lapses, so
a freshly loaded tab knows when to refresh without paying a failed request
first. ``None`` for a credential with no session expiry to report.

MemberCredentialCounts.title: MemberCredentialCounts
MemberCredentialCounts.description:
How a per-user row's members stand with their own credentials — the one
number an admin needs to know that the row works for everybody but Dana.

has_shared_secret.title: Has Shared Secret
has_shared_secret.description: Compatibility flag: true when any primary or named shared credential is stored.

has_primary_secret.title: Has Primary Secret
has_primary_secret.description: True when the shared credential bundle includes a primary value.

MemberTeamConnection.title: MemberTeamConnection
MemberTeamConnection.description:
The member sync-down shape — full definition, NO secrets. The member's
daemon reconciles these into the workspace (suggested / auto-added).

MembershipListResponse.title: MembershipListResponse
MembershipListResponse.description:
`GET /auth/memberships`: the caller's active memberships, most recently
used first, then any pending ones, and the org the calling credential is
in.

MembershipRead.title: MembershipRead
MembershipRead.description:
One org the caller belongs to and can switch into, or, when ``status``
is ``pending``, one that provisioned them and waits for them to join.

MessageResponse.title: MessageResponse
MessageResponse.description: Generic 'OK' response for endpoints that return only an acknowledgement.

MfaCodeRequest.title: MfaCodeRequest
MfaCodeRequest.description: A 6-digit TOTP or a backup code (used to confirm enrollment / disable MFA).

MfaConfirmResponse.title: MfaConfirmResponse
MfaConfirmResponse.description: Activation result — the single-use backup codes, shown exactly once.

MfaEnrollRequest.title: MfaEnrollRequest
MfaEnrollRequest.description:
Step-up proof for turning MFA on.

Optional: a caller whose session was minted within
``_MFA_ENROLL_AUTH_FRESHNESS`` has already proved a factor and sends nothing.
An older session on a password account has to re-present the password here.

MfaEnrollResponse.title: MfaEnrollResponse
MfaEnrollResponse.description:
One-time enrollment payload — the secret + otpauth URI to add to an
authenticator app. Persisted PENDING; activated by /mfa/confirm.

ModelProviderRead.title: ModelProviderRead
ModelProviderRead.description: One provider card. NEVER carries a secret — only presence + a hint.

ModelProviderUpdateRequest.title: ModelProviderUpdateRequest
ModelProviderUpdateRequest.description:
Upsert one provider's config. Secret fields omitted/blank KEEP the stored
value; changing ``base_url`` requires re-entering the key (anti-exfiltration
— a stored valid key must never be silently repointed at a new endpoint).

NameFlagsWire.title: NameFlagsWire
NameFlagsWire.description: What the server knows about how this name behaves on a client's filesystem.

NotebookConnection.title: NotebookConnection
NotebookConnection.description:
One connection a SQL cell of the notebook may name.

``name`` is the connection's name, what a cell stores
(``alkera.sql(..., connection="<name>")``) and what the kernel resolves
on the box; it is also how the connection is shown. ``can_use`` is the
server's answer for this reader and this connection, with ``reason`` one
sentence when it is no.

NotebookConnections.title: NotebookConnections
NotebookConnections.description:
``GET .../connections``: what the notebook's SQL cells may name. Empty
for a notebook in no workspace, whose kernel resolves no connection.

NotebookEditor.title: NotebookEditor
NotebookEditor.description:
``GET .../editor``: where the notebook editor opens a notebook, or a
new notebook in a folder. ``chat_id`` is the chat whose workspace pane
runs it: the chat whose own folder holds it, or, in a workspace's folder,
the chat a wake of that workspace goes through. ``None`` where no kernel
can run (outside every workspace and chat folder, or in an ended one) or
where the caller may send in no chat that would run it.

NotebookOpsRequest.title: NotebookOpsRequest
NotebookOpsRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/notebooks/{drive_id}/{item_id}/ops``: a batch applied
atomically on a Loro peer at ``base_token`` (the head when absent).

NotebookView.title: NotebookView
NotebookView.description:
A notebook as a reader sees it: its document, its kernel and who is
where. The one definition: the engine's client, the agent tools, the
platform's notebook route and the web client (through the generated API
types) all use this shape.

OAuthProvidersResponse.title: OAuthProvidersResponse
OAuthProvidersResponse.description:
Platform-enabled external-login providers, for rendering sign-in buttons.

Note: this is the *platform* configuration (which providers have credentials
wired up). Per-org `allow_login_*` gating is enforced server-side at the
callback — the login page can't know the org before sign-in.

OAuthRegisterContext.title: OAuthRegisterContext
OAuthRegisterContext.description:
Prefill data for the SPA register screen, derived from a signed ticket.

The backend always trusts the ticket (not the client) for email/provider —
these are display-only hints.

OAuthRegisterRequest.title: OAuthRegisterRequest
OAuthRegisterRequest.description:
Complete an OAuth-initiated registration.

`oauth_ticket` is the signed ticket minted by the OAuth callback; it carries
the verified email/provider/subject. The user supplies (and may edit) their
name, and chooses an org exactly like email/password signup: exactly one of
`org_name` (new org, becomes Org Admin) or `invite_token` (join via invite).
When the ticket itself carries an invite, that wins.

ObjectFacet.title: ObjectFacet
ObjectFacet.description:
A row-backed object (a chat, a query, a board) rendered as a node.

``title`` is the object's own CURRENT title, which is not the node's name.
The name was minted from the title the day the node was created and is a
filesystem name ever since — an untitled chat is a uuid, and renaming the
chat afterwards does not rename the folder. A surface that renders the node
name therefore shows ``3952c9e2-….alkerachat`` for a conversation the person
has been calling something else all morning. Empty when the object has no
title (or, on a record written before 1.1.0, when nobody asked).

ObjectPayloadFailure.title: ObjectPayloadFailure
ObjectPayloadFailure.description:
The daemon saying the payload behind a promoted result is not coming.

Without it the object would wait in ``pending_upload`` forever, reading as
"Saving…" on its page and "0 rows" in the list, so the reason is recorded
on the object itself.

ObjectPayloadUpload.title: ObjectPayloadUpload
ObjectPayloadUpload.description: The daemon's promote upload: the envelope and the receipt that proves it.

ObjectRowsPage.title: ObjectRowsPage
ObjectRowsPage.description:
One page of a result's rows, mediated by authz — never a storage URL.

``columns`` are the display labels and ``keys`` the stable column names
behind them, in the same order: a chart's encoding names a key, so a
renderer binds by ``keys`` and shows ``columns``, and a rename can never
detach the chart from its data.

storage_rate_per_gb_month_nanos.title: Storage Rate Per Gb Month Nanos

OfferingAdminRead.title: OfferingAdminRead
OfferingAdminRead.description: An offering as a platform admin sees it. Platform only.

storage_rate_per_gb_month_nanos.title: Storage Rate Per Gb Month Nanos
Storage Rate Per Gb Month Nanos

OfferingUpdate.title: OfferingUpdate
OfferingUpdate.description:
A change to an offering; fields not sent are left as they are.
``retired`` true retires it, false brings it back. Platform only.

OperationConflictWire.title: OperationConflictWire
OperationConflictWire.description: A collision the operation resolved, as the pair of node ids involved.

OperationErrorWire.title: OperationErrorWire
OperationErrorWire.description: One item the operation could not do, by id and code — never by name.

OrgChatInsight.title: OrgChatInsight
OrgChatInsight.description: One of the org's chats as the admin activity list shows it.

OrgComputeAssignmentUpdate.title: OrgComputeAssignmentUpdate
OrgComputeAssignmentUpdate.description: Point an org's chats at one dedicated box, or return it to the pool.

OrgCreatedResponse.title: OrgCreatedResponse
OrgCreatedResponse.description: The org just created, for the client to switch into.

OrgIssue.title: OrgIssue
OrgIssue.description:
A thing that went wrong in one of the org's chats.

``error``: a turn that ended in an error, or a session that reported one.
``refusal``: the model refused. ``denied``: a person or policy rejected a
permission ask. ``machine_refused``: the bound machine said it cannot
publish the chat.

OrgLiveEditingRead.title: OrgLiveEditingRead
OrgLiveEditingRead.description: Where an org stands on live editing, as the platform sees it.

OrgLiveEditingUpdate.title: OrgLiveEditingUpdate
OrgLiveEditingUpdate.description:
The org's own setting: ``true`` or ``false`` wins over the deployment's
in either direction; ``null`` clears it, so the org follows the
deployment again. The key is required, so an empty body changes
nothing by accident; only a JSON boolean is a setting (``"off"`` or
``0`` is a 422, never read as false).

OrgMachineGrant.title: OrgMachineGrant
OrgMachineGrant.description: A machine Alkera gives an org, free until ``free_until``. Platform only.

OrgMachineUpdate.title: OrgMachineUpdate
OrgMachineUpdate.description:
Fields not sent are left as they are (read ``model_fields_set``); a
field sent as ``null`` clears it where clearing means something
(``idle_stop_minutes``: never stop; ``monthly_cap_nanos``: no cap).

OrgRead.title: OrgRead
OrgRead.description:
Same shape as TeamRead — separate name communicates intent at the
admin route surface — plus, on the detail read, the org's storage picture.

OrgSettingsRead.title: OrgSettingsRead
OrgSettingsRead.description: Org-wide settings. A missing row reads as all-defaults (see service).

OrgSettingsUpdate.title: OrgSettingsUpdate
OrgSettingsUpdate.description:
Partial update — only provided fields change (``model_fields_set``
distinguishes an explicit null, which CLEARS a value, from an absent one).

OrgStorageLimitUpdate.title: OrgStorageLimitUpdate
OrgStorageLimitUpdate.description: ``null`` is an explicit "unlimited"; a figure is a ceiling in bytes.

OrgStorageRead.title: OrgStorageRead
OrgStorageRead.description: An org's storage picture as the platform sees it.

OrgUpdate.title: OrgUpdate
OrgUpdate.description:
Admin-side org edit — currently just the display name (the root team's
name).

OrgUserRead.title: OrgUserRead
OrgUserRead.description:
One colleague as the organization directory shows them.

Deliberately narrower than ``UserRead``. A read of SOMEONE ELSE must not
carry their security posture: ``mfa_enabled`` and ``has_password`` together
name exactly which colleagues have no second factor and which sign in with a
password — a ranked target list for a phishing or credential-stuffing run —
while ``platform_role`` marks who is Alkera staff inside the tenant and
``email_verified_at`` who never proved their address. A caller's own posture
is still theirs to read, on ``GET /api/v1/auth/me``.

``display_name`` is the name this org shows for the person: the one its
admin, IdP or SCIM set on their membership, else their own name. No field
names an org or carries anything another org knows about them.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description:
What a settled verification found. ``unsupported`` means the connector
cannot be checked from this vantage; ``infrastructure`` means Alkera could
not run the check at all (no guard library, an unreadable ciphertext, a
worker that never picked it up) — neither is the customer's fault.

OutputsClearRequest.title: OutputsClearRequest
OutputsClearRequest.description:
Clear these cells' outputs for everyone, or every cell's when
``cell_ids`` is ``None``.

PatchItem.title: PatchItem
PatchItem.description: The `PATCH` body: a rename, a move, an attrs change, or any combination.

PersonalBoxRead.title: PersonalBoxRead
PersonalBoxRead.description:
One box on the caller's own hardware, as its person sees it: what it is
called, the org it serves them in, when it was set up and last spoke, and
whether its standing was taken away. ``id`` is the credential's id, the
one the revoke route names. Never the secret.

PlacesRead.title: PlacesRead
PlacesRead.description:
The caller's own home and the named folders inside it.

Every field is nullable because every one of them is answered by a *read*
when ``ensure`` did not name it: a member who has never saved a template
has no ``Chat Templates`` folder, and inventing one on a page load would
put a folder in their drive that they did not make.

PlatformMachineRead.title: PlatformMachineRead
PlatformMachineRead.description: One platform box: its credential, and its registration when it has one.

PlatformRole.title: PlatformRole
PlatformRole.description:
Cross-tenant platform staff role. Nullable on `users` — most users
have no platform role at all.

PlatformRoleUpdate.title: PlatformRoleUpdate
PlatformRoleUpdate.description: ADMIN-only — set or clear a user's platform_role.

chat_model_defaulted.title: Chat Model Defaulted
chat_model_defaulted.description: True when `default_chat_model` / `default_chat_effort` in this answer are the platform default rather than the caller's own pick — they never chose one, or the one they chose is no longer offered. A client that edits the document shows this as 'no preference' and must not save the answered model back as a choice.

PreferencesRead.title: PreferencesRead
PreferencesRead.description:
The caller's stored preferences, whole.

A free-form object on purpose: :class:`Preferences` allows unknown fields so
a newer client's key survives an older one's read, and a typed mirror here
would be the thing that dropped it.

PreferencesUpdate.title: PreferencesUpdate
PreferencesUpdate.description:
The fields to apply. MERGED onto what is stored, never a replacement —
so a key a newer client wrote survives an older client's save.

``extra="forbid"`` where the persisted :class:`Preferences` allows extras,
and the two are not in tension: the STORED document must keep a field it
cannot name (a newer client wrote it), while a REQUEST that misses the
envelope has nothing to preserve and everything to lose. A client PATCHing
the flat ``{"default_permission_mode": …}`` instead of
``{"preferences": {…}}`` gets a 422 rather than a 200 with an empty merge
that silently drops the setting.

Presence.title: Presence
Presence.description: Someone who is in a cell now (the rule is ``document/editing.py``).

PrincipalRef.title: PrincipalRef
PrincipalRef.description:
Who a grant is for: a ``user``, a ``team`` or the ``org`` itself.

The kind is an open registry, so a kind the server has not registered is a
422 rather than a row nothing can resolve. An ``org`` grant names the
caller's own org; any other id is a 422 too. A ``user`` or ``team`` id that
is not a principal of the caller's org (another org's, a stranger, an id
never issued) is a 404, the same answer for every one of them, so the route
never confirms who exists outside the org.

Provider.title: Provider
Provider.description: Upstream LLM provider a request is fulfilled by (route + cost keying).

ProviderStatus.title: ProviderStatus
ProviderStatus.description:
Whether this deployment can start machines at one provider, and, when it
cannot, the settings it is missing.

PublicConfigResponse.title: PublicConfigResponse
PublicConfigResponse.description: Branding the SPA needs before a user is authenticated.

RealtimeEventType.title: RealtimeEventType
RealtimeEventType.description:
The events a client may receive over the portal's event stream.

Every :class:`EventType` except those that exist for the server's own
use: ``doc.op`` (a doc-sync envelope, delivered over the socket gateway to
a channel subscriber and never as a bare invalidation), ``notebook.event``
(a notebook kernel's events, delivered the same way) and
``authz.decision`` (an audit record). This enum reaches the OpenAPI schema
through the stream's response model, so a client-side handler map can be
checked exhaustive against it; a test pins it equal to the registry minus
those two.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: The DocEnvelope schema version this server writes.

close_codes.title: Close Codes
close_codes.description: Close-code names to their numeric codes.

channel_pattern.title: Channel Pattern
channel_pattern.description: The regular expression a channel name must match.

RealtimeProtocolDescriptor.title: RealtimeProtocolDescriptor
RealtimeProtocolDescriptor.description:
``GET /api/v1/ws/protocol``: the vocabulary this server speaks, so a
client can pin itself against it.

Reauth.title: Reauth
Reauth.description: What fixes a credential that needs re-authentication.

RebaseRequest.title: RebaseRequest
RebaseRequest.description:
``POST .../rebase``: an editor's update written in ``epoch`` that never
reached it (the document's history restarted first), standard base64 of
the Loro update bytes. The server carries it into the current epoch cell
by cell.

RebaseResult.title: RebaseResult
RebaseResult.description: The token of the document's state once the update is in.

RecipientInvitationRead.title: RecipientInvitationRead
RecipientInvitationRead.description:
One of the caller's own pending invitations, as the recipient sees it.

Carries the destination by name (a team in another organization is not in
the caller's team list, so the client cannot resolve it), who sent it, and —
when the account cannot accept it — the refusal the accept route would give.
A refused invitation is still listed so its recipient can read why and
decline it; only the owner of the address ever sees this shape.

ReleaseBody.title: ReleaseBody
ReleaseBody.description:
The hand-back. ``unsyncedCount`` is how many files the holder still had
queued when its drain ran out, and ``unsyncedPaths`` names up to
:data:`RELEASE_MAX_UNSYNCED_PATHS` of them; the count is recorded on the
lease, the paths are the holder's report and are not stored.

ReplaceCell.title: ReplaceCell
ReplaceCell.description:
Set a cell's whole text; applied as a diff, so concurrent typing in the
parts it leaves alone survives.

RestoreRequest.title: RestoreRequest
RestoreRequest.description: Where a restore should land. Omit ``parentId`` for the original place.

RoleOption.title: RoleOption
RoleOption.description: A rung the caller may hand out here, with what it is called.

RunActor.title: RunActor
RunActor.description:
Who asked for a run: the person or agent whose action caused it (for
a widget-triggered or autorun run too), ``system`` only for what nobody
asked for.

RunRequest.title: RunRequest
RunRequest.description:
``POST .../runs``. ``frontier`` is the document token the requester
holds: the run waits (up to 2 s) for the document to include it, then
takes its targets' text from there.

SaveAsTemplate.title: SaveAsTemplate
SaveAsTemplate.description:
Save a chat as the starting point for the next one.

Everything but the chat is optional because the server can answer for all
of it: the title from the chat, the brief from its transcript, and the
destination from the caller's own ``Chat Templates`` folder. A reader who
wants none of those defaults overrides the one they care about.

ScimTokenResponse.title: ScimTokenResponse
ScimTokenResponse.description: The freshly-minted SCIM bearer token — shown ONCE; only its hash is stored.

SecurityEventRead.title: SecurityEventRead
SecurityEventRead.description:
One event in the caller's security log. ``org_team_id`` is the org the
caller's session was in when it happened, when there was one.

SessionRead.title: SessionRead
SessionRead.description:
One live session in `GET /auth/sessions`. Never includes a token value.

A browser session is a refresh-token FAMILY: `jti` carries the family id,
`issued_at` is when it signed in, `expires_at` its absolute expiry, and
`client` what the browser said it was. A CLI token is its own row, keyed by
its real `jti`. `current` flags the session making the request (so a UI can
avoid offering to revoke the user out from under themselves without warning).

SetCellMeta.title: SetCellMeta
SetCellMeta.description:
Change a SQL or Markdown cell's settings; a key set to ``None`` goes
back to its default (a SQL cell with no ``connection`` runs in DuckDB).

ShareCandidate.title: ShareCandidate
ShareCandidate.description: Someone the caller may name on a share of this node.

SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest
SignupRequest.description:
Minimal signup: only email + password are required. Name and org are
finished on the complete-profile step.

Org selection (mutually exclusive — never both):
- `invite_token` set → join the inviter's org with the invitation's role.
- `org_name` set → create a new org with that name (the caller becomes Org
  Admin). Optional: omitting it creates a new *unnamed* org the caller names
  on complete-profile.

Names are optional (the empty-string "profile incomplete" sentinel) and
collected on complete-profile; a caller that already knows them (apps/web,
OAuth) may still send them here.

SpecialFacet.title: SpecialFacet
SpecialFacet.description:
A device, fifo or socket node.

``rdev`` is the POSIX device number a materializer needs to recreate the
node; the server never opens one, so nothing here is followed.

SseEventData.title: SseEventData
SseEventData.description:
The body of one ``event: <type>`` frame; ``id:`` on the frame is the
outbox row id the client resumes from.

The optional fields below are the only things a frame carries beyond
the entity it names, and every one of them is an ID the reader could have
asked for anyway. They exist so a client can narrow WHICH cached read it
re-takes: a folder mounted live has to know that this node sits in the
folder it is showing, and a file open in a tab has to know its own node
moved, or every frame costs a refetch of everything. They stay optional
because plenty of writers genuinely do not hold them — a client handed
``None`` refreshes wider, which is slower and never wrong.

SshEndpointRead.title: SshEndpointRead
SshEndpointRead.description: Where an added machine is reached. Never the credential.

SshMachineTarget.title: SshMachineTarget
SshMachineTarget.description: A host and how to sign in to it.

SshMachineTestRead.title: SshMachineTestRead
SshMachineTestRead.description:
What a connection test found. ``reachable`` false carries the reason in
``error_code`` and ``message``; the facts are then empty.

SsoConnectionRead.title: SsoConnectionRead
SsoConnectionRead.description:
The org's SSO config for the admin screen. The OIDC client secret + SAML
cert are NEVER returned — only whether they're stored. For SAML, the SP
values the org admin must register with their IdP are surfaced.

SsoDomainsRead.title: SsoDomainsRead
SsoDomainsRead.description: The email domains assigned to an org's SSO connection.

SsoDomainsUpdate.title: SsoDomainsUpdate
SsoDomainsUpdate.description:
The org's whole set of SSO email domains, replacing what it had. Set by
platform staff only.

SsoExemptMember.title: SsoExemptMember
SsoExemptMember.description:
A break-glass member of this org: may sign in without the org's IdP even
where the org enforces SSO. The flag is on their membership in this org and
has no effect anywhere else.

SsoLinkConfirmResponse.title: SsoLinkConfirmResponse
SsoLinkConfirmResponse.description:
`POST /auth/sso-link/confirm`. ``joined`` is whether the person is now
an active member of the org; when not, ``message`` says what to do next.

SsoLinkRead.title: SsoLinkRead
SsoLinkRead.description:
`GET /auth/sso-link`: the org whose single sign-on is waiting to be
linked to the signed-in identity, and the address its IdP asserted,
masked.

StatusAction.title: StatusAction
StatusAction.description: The one thing the reader may do about the state, with the button's words.

StatusFact.title: StatusFact
StatusFact.description: Where one thing stands, as every surface draws it.

StockRead.title: StockRead
StockRead.description:
Whether an offering can be bought now, as the server decided it
(``alkera_core.compute.stock.offer_verdict``): the stock of the size it
sells, and a sentence saying why not when it cannot. Clients render it.

StoredNotebook.title: StoredNotebook
StoredNotebook.description:
A notebook file as it is stored: its cells as the file holds them, each
with the outputs saved beside it. Read with no kernel and no live
document, so a reader who may only see the file gets it as a notebook.

SwitchOrgRequest.title: SwitchOrgRequest
SwitchOrgRequest.description:
`POST /auth/refresh/org`: the org to switch this browser into. Checked
against the caller's own active memberships; it never selects anything a
membership does not already grant.

SymlinkFacet.title: SymlinkFacet
SymlinkFacet.description:
A symlink's stored target and what its text points at.

``kind`` is the tree's own vocabulary (``file_nodes.symlink_kind``:
``relative`` — resolved against this directory, ``canonical`` — an absolute
path in the org's namespace that a materializer rewrites to the local root,
``host`` — a path on some machine, stored and recreated verbatim, never
followed server-side). The wire maps 1:1 to what is stored, so
``POST …/children`` takes the kind it reads back. 1.0.0 spelled the three
``internal | external | absolute``; the migration maps them forward.

TableColumn.title: TableColumn
TableColumn.description:
One column of a table page: its name and the frame library's own name
for its type (``Date``, ``Decimal(precision=4, scale=2)``, ``Int64``).

TablePage.title: TablePage
TablePage.description:
``GET .../cells/{cell_id}/table``: one page of a table output.

The table page the kernel makes (``_alkera_kernel.tables``), unchanged:
the same ``schema``, ``rows``, ``total_rows`` and ``offset`` a cell's
table output carries for its first page, so a reader takes every page
the same way. ``rows`` is one list per row in column order, each cell
already plain JSON (a date as ISO text, a decimal as its text).

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Primary shared credential; empty when the bundle contains only named values.

TeamConnectionCredentialLease.title: TeamConnectionCredentialLease
TeamConnectionCredentialLease.description:
A short-lived lease of a shared credential bundle.

The daemon holds it in memory only and re-leases on expiry; the backend
refuses the next lease when the connection is disabled, flipped off shared
mode, or deleted. Every lease is audited.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Primary shared credential; empty when the bundle contains only named values.

TeamConnectionCredentialResponse.title: TeamConnectionCredentialResponse
TeamConnectionCredentialResponse.description:
The decrypted shared credential bundle for an entitled member.

Each value is written to its own chmod-600 file locally. Every fetch is
audited; ``credential_version`` keys the bundle's local copy.

has_shared_secret.title: Has Shared Secret
has_shared_secret.description: Compatibility flag: true when any primary or named shared credential is stored.

has_primary_secret.title: Has Primary Secret
has_primary_secret.description: True when the shared credential bundle includes a primary value.

TeamConnectionRead.title: TeamConnectionRead
TeamConnectionRead.description: One preconfigured connection, admin/portal view. No secret material.

TeamConnectionRotateSecretRequest.title: TeamConnectionRotateSecretRequest
TeamConnectionRotateSecretRequest.description:
Rotate only the primary shared credential.

Named roles change through the connection edit that owns their endpoint.
This distinct verb records primary rotations and bumps the bundle version.

TeamConnectionUpsertRequest.title: TeamConnectionUpsertRequest
TeamConnectionUpsertRequest.description:
Create/update a preconfigured connection (team admins).

``fields`` is the COMPLETE raw form input — every value, including the ones
the admin keeps to themselves — because the server can only verify a whole
connection, and this is the one moment somebody holds one. It builds and
test-dials that, then stores none of it: what persists is the subset named
by ``shared_fields``, raw, plus each independently encrypted credential role
that was shared. A shared secret left blank on edit preserves that same
primary or named role; a role is retired when the edited build no longer
declares it, including when an optional feature is disabled.
``oauth_client_secret`` is likewise write-only, with None meaning keep.

TeamMemberRead.title: TeamMemberRead
TeamMemberRead.description:
One person's standing on one team, with their identity and the team's
name, so the member table needs no client-side join.

A person stands on a team two ways, and the two are not exclusive: a
membership row written on the team itself (``direct_role``), and admin
reaching the team from a team above it (``descent_role``, carried from
``descent_from_team_*`` — the nearest ancestor holding the admin row). A
person can hold both; a person can hold only one. ``role`` is what they
hold here once descent is applied — admin when either side is admin, else
the direct row's role — and ``effective_role`` names the same value for
what it is. Descent is decided server-side so no client recomputes it.

TeamRole.title: TeamRole

TextEdit.title: TextEdit
TextEdit.description:
Replace ``old`` with ``new`` in a cell's text. ``occurrence`` (1-based)
picks one of several matches; without it, ``old`` must match once.

TokenType.title: TokenType
TokenType.description:
Kind of auth token recorded in `auth_tokens`.

`session` = short-lived cookie JWT (SPA); `cli` = long-lived Bearer JWT
(the `alkera` CLI + daemon). Same JWT shape; differ only in TTL + origin.

TrashEmptyResult.title: TrashEmptyResult
TrashEmptyResult.description:
What one sweep of the trash did, and what it left behind.

``skipped`` exists because emptying is decided per deletion: a root the
caller may not delete stays, and an answer naming only what it removed reads
as "the trash is empty" when it is not.

TrashEntryWire.title: TrashEntryWire
TrashEntryWire.description: One trashed root, with how long is left before the purge takes it.

TrashPage.title: TrashPage
TrashPage.description: One marker page of the trash view.

TreeBatch.title: TreeBatch
TreeBatch.description: One flush of the holder's metadata queue.

TreeCreate.title: TreeCreate
TreeCreate.description: The `POST …/tree` body: the folder skeleton of a dropped directory.

TreeEntry.title: TreeEntry
TreeEntry.description: One change under the leased folder, as the holder saw it on disk.

UnmanagedMachine.title: UnmanagedMachine
UnmanagedMachine.description:
A machine a provider bills this account for that no allocation row owns:
started by hand, or left behind. Read-only; the console never acts on it.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description:
Self-service or admin-driven update. Cannot change platform_role here
— that lives behind /admin/v1/users/{id}/platform_role.

On your own account the names, email and password are your identity's.
``current_password`` / ``mfa_code`` are the step-up proof required to change
either credential-grade field (``email``, ``password``); they are ignored for
a name-only edit.

An org admin editing a member sets the name the org shows for them
(``display_name``, or ``first_name`` + ``last_name`` combined), on their
membership in the org; the person's own name is never written.

VersionList.title: VersionList
VersionList.description: A file's whole history, oldest first.

VersionWire.title: VersionWire
VersionWire.description: One row of a file's history. `isHead` is the version the node points at.

WidgetAssetResolved.title: WidgetAssetResolved
WidgetAssetResolved.description: ``GET .../widget-assets/resolve``: the hash of a widget module's code.

WorkspaceCreate.title: WorkspaceCreate
WorkspaceCreate.description: A new project workspace, with a folder of its own.

WorkspaceDeletion.title: WorkspaceDeletion
WorkspaceDeletion.description:
Where a deleted workspace's deletion stands. The workspace and its chats
are gone from every read the moment it is deleted; ``deleting`` means the
background pass is still ending its chats and trashing their folders.

WorkspaceObjectUpdate.title: WorkspaceObjectUpdate
WorkspaceObjectUpdate.description:
``expected_version`` is required and never optional: a write that does
not say which row it read is a write that did not read one.

WorkspaceRead.title: WorkspaceRead
WorkspaceRead.description: One workspace as a list or a detail view shows it.

WorkspaceUpdate.title: WorkspaceUpdate
WorkspaceUpdate.description:
A rename. ``expected_version`` is required: a write that does not say
which row it read is a write that did not read one.

expires_in.title: Expires In
expires_in.description: Seconds until the ticket dies unused.

path.title: Path
path.description: The socket path to connect to.

WsTicketResponse.title: WsTicketResponse
WsTicketResponse.description:
``POST /api/v1/ws/tickets``: a single-use, short-lived credential for
one socket handshake. A box a release behind parses it, so a field
this build does not know is ignored, never refused.
